questions.stem:
A random sample of 35 homeowners was taken from each of the villages Greenslax and Penville and their ages were recorded. The results are summarised in the back-to-back stem and leaf diagram below.

Totals Greenslax Penville Totals
(2)          8 7 | 2 | 5 5 6 7 8 8 9          (7)
(3)        9 8 7 | 3 | 1 1 1 2 3 4 4 5 6 7 9   (11)
(4)      4 4 4 0 | 4 | 0 1 2 4 7               (5)
(5)    6 6 5 2 2 | 5 | 0 0 5 5 5               (5)
(7)  8 6 5 4 2 1 1 | 6 | 2 5 6 6               (4)
(8) 8 6 6 6 4 3 1 1 | 7 | 0 5                  (2)
(5)      9 8 4 3 2 | 8 |                       (0)
(1)            4 | 9 | 9                       (1)

Key: 7 | 3 | 1 means 37 years for Greenslax and 31 years for Penville

Some of the quartiles for these two distributions are given in the table below.

$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline & \text{Greenslax} & \text{Penville}\\\hline \text{Lower quartile, }Q_1 & a & 31\\\hline \text{Median, }Q_2 & 64 & 39\\\hline \text{Upper quartile, }Q_3 & b & 55\\\hline\end{array}$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the value of $a$ and the value of $b$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme: $a=44$ B1; $b=76$ B1. These answers may be in or near the table.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
An outlier is a value that falls either

more than $1.5\times(Q_3-Q_1)$ above $Q_3$

or more than $1.5\times(Q_3-Q_1)$ below $Q_1$

(b) On the graph paper opposite draw a box plot to represent the data from Penville. Show clearly any outliers.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $55+1.5(55-31)=91$ [and $31-1.5(55-31)=-5$]. B1: box with whiskers (condone missing median). B1: 25, 31, 39, 55, RH whisker to end at 75 or 91. Two RH whiskers is B0. A1: only one outlier plotted at 99. Allow cross to be vertically displaced. If the RH whisker goes to 99 (2nd B0) and A0 even if outlier is identified since we require a horizontal 'gap' between RH whisker and outlier.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- A fully correct box plot scores 4/4. If not fully correct apply scheme and need evidence for M1. If two box plots are seen ignore the one for Greenslax. If not on graph paper M1 max for (b)
- M1 for sight of $55+1.5(55-31)$ or 91 seen (possibly implied by RH whisker of box plot) May be implied by a fully correct box plot
- Accuracy must be to within 0.5 of a square so e.g. lower quartile at 30 or 32 is OK

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) State the skewness of each distribution. Justify your answers.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: Greenslax: $[Q_2-Q_1=20, Q_3-Q_2=12$ or $(Q_2-Q_1)>(Q_3-Q_2)]\Rightarrow$ $-$ve (skew). B1: Penville: $[Q_2-Q_1=8, Q_3-Q_2=16$ or $(Q_3-Q_2)>(Q_2-Q_1)]\Rightarrow$ +ve (skew). ddB1: justification that is consistent, dependent on 1st and 2nd B marks being scored. Don't insist on seeing 'skew' so just -ve and +ve will do. Treat 'correlation' as ISW.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- We must be able to tell which is which but labels may be implied by their values but not simply from $Q_3-Q_2>Q_2-Q_1$. If there is just one, unlabelled comment assume Penville.
- Justification for both based on: quartiles, median relative to quartiles, or "tail"
- If only values for $Q_3-Q_2$ etc are given they should be correct ft for Greenslax and correct for Penville
- If values for Greenslax imply +ve skew then 1st B0 and 3rd B0

parts.text:
The mark, $x$, scored by each student who sat a statistics examination is coded using

$y = 1.4x-20$

The coded marks have mean 60.8 and standard deviation 6.60

Find the mean and the standard deviation of $x$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: mean $=\dfrac{60.8+20}{1.4}$ or $60.8=1.4x-20$ (o.e.). A1: $=57.7142\ldots$, awrt 57.7. M1: standard deviation $=\dfrac{6.60}{1.4}$ or $6.60=1.4x$. A1: $=4.7142\ldots$, awrt 4.71. Note: $6.60^2=1.4^2x^2$ is M0 until we see them take a square root. Correct answer only is 2/2 for each pair.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- 1st M1 sub. 60.8 for $y$ into a correct equation. Allow use of $x$ or any other letter or expression for mean
- 1st A1 for awrt 57.7 or $\frac{404}{7}$ (o.e.).
- 2nd M1 sub. 6.60 or 6.6 for $y$ and ignoring the 20. Allow use of $x$ or any other letter or expression for st. dev.
- 2nd A1 for awrt 4.71 or $\frac{33}{7}$ (o.e.).

questions.stem:
In a factory, three machines, $J$, $K$ and $L$, are used to make biscuits.

Machine $J$ makes 25% of the biscuits.

Machine $K$ makes 45% of the biscuits.

The rest of the biscuits are made by machine $L$.

It is known that 2% of the biscuits made by machine $J$ are broken, 3% of the biscuits made by machine $K$ are broken and 5% of the biscuits made by machine $L$ are broken.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Draw a tree diagram to illustrate all the possible outcomes and associated probabilities.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: (3+6) tree drawn with 0.25, 0.45, 0.02, 0.03, 0.05 on correct branches. A1: for 0.3, 0.98, 0.97, 0.95 on the correct branches and labels, condone missing $B'$s. Allow 3+6 tree diagram with the 6 correct 'end' probs and labels to get 2/2 (1st, 3rd, 5th gets M1). Correct answer only scores full marks for parts (b), (c) and (d).
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Allow fractions or percentages throughout this question
- When using "their probability $p$" for M1 and A1ft they must have $0<p<1$

parts.label: b
parts.text:
A biscuit is selected at random.

(b) Calculate the probability that the biscuit is made by machine $J$ and is not broken.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $0.25\times 0.98$. A1: $=0.245$ (or exact equiv. e.g. $\frac{49}{200}$).
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 for $0.25\times$ 'their 0.98' o.e.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Calculate the probability that the biscuit is broken.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $0.25\times 0.02+0.45\times 0.03+0.3\times 0.05$. A1: $=0.0335$ (or exact equiv. e.g. $\frac{67}{2000}$). Or $1-(0.25\times\text{their }0.98+0.45\times\text{their }0.97+0.3\times\text{their }0.95)$.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 for $0.25\times$their $0.02+0.45\times$their $0.03+$their $0.3\times$their 0.05 Condone 1 transcription error.

parts.label: d
parts.text:
(d) Given that the biscuit is broken, find the probability that it was not made by machine $K$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme: $[\mathrm{P}(J\cup L\,|\,B)]=\dfrac{0.25\times0.02+0.3\times0.05}{0.0335}$ or $\dfrac{0.0335-0.45\times0.03}{0.0335}$ M1A1ft. A1: $=0.5970\ldots$, awrt 0.597 (or $\frac{40}{67}$ or exact equiv.). M1: for use of conditional probability with their (c) as denominator. Also exactly 2 products on num' and at least one correct (or correct ft) or their (c) minus one of the products from their (c). Ignore an incorrect expression inside their probability statement. A1ft: for $\dfrac{0.25\times\text{their }0.02+\text{their }0.3\times\text{their }0.05}{\text{their}(c)}$ or $\dfrac{\text{their}(c)-0.45\times\text{their }0.03}{\text{their}(c)}$ or $\dfrac{0.02}{\text{their}(c)}$.

questions.stem:
The times, in seconds, spent in a queue at a supermarket by 85 randomly selected customers, are summarised in the table below.

$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline \text{Time (seconds)} & \text{Number of customers, }f\\\hline 0-30 & 2\\\hline 30-60 & 10\\\hline 60-70 & 17\\\hline 70-80 & 25\\\hline 80-100 & 25\\\hline 100-150 & 6\\\hline\end{array}$

A histogram was drawn to represent these data. The 30 − 60 group was represented by a bar of width 1.5 cm and height 1 cm.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the width and the height of the 70 − 80 group.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: 70 − 80 group - width 0.5 (cm). M1: $1.5\text{ cm}^2$ is 10 customers or $3.75\text{ cm}^2$ is 25 customers or $0.5c=3.75$ or $\dfrac{2.5}{\frac{1}{3}}$. A1: 70 − 80 group - height 7.5 (cm).
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 for one of the given statements or any method where "their width" $\times$ "their height" = 3.75. Correct height scores M1A1 independent of width so B0M1A1 is possible.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Use linear interpolation to estimate the median of this distribution.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Median $=(70)+\dfrac{13.5}{25}\times10$, allow $(n+1)=(70)+\dfrac{14}{25}\times10$. A1: $=75.4$ (or if using $(n+1)$ allow 75.6).
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 for a correct fraction: $+\frac{k}{25}\times10$ where $k=13.5$ or 14 for $(n+1)$ case.
- NB may work down so look out for $(80)-\frac{11.5}{25}\times10$ etc Beware: $69.5+\frac{13.5}{25}\times11=75.44$ (but M0)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
Given that $x$ denotes the midpoint of each group in the table and

$\sum fx=6460 \qquad \sum fx^2=529\,400$

(c) calculate an estimate for

(i) the mean,

(ii) the standard deviation,

for the above data.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(i) B1: Mean $=\dfrac{6460}{85}=76$. (ii) M1: $\sigma=\sqrt{\dfrac{529400}{85}-76^2}$. A1: $=21.2658\ldots$ ($s=21.3920$), awrt 21.3.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 for a correct expression with square root, ft their mean. A1 for awrt 21.3 or, if clearly using $s$ allow awrt 21.4. Must be evaluated...no surds.

parts.label: d
parts.text:
One measure of skewness is given by

coefficient of skewness $=\dfrac{3(\text{mean}-\text{median})}{\text{standard deviation}}$

(d) Evaluate this coefficient and comment on the skewness of these data.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Coeff' of skewness $=\dfrac{3(76-75.4)}{21.2658\ldots}=0.08464\ldots$. A1: awrt 0.08 (awrt 0.06 for 75.6). B1ft: There is (very slight) positive skew or the data is almost symmetrical (or both). Allow 'symmetrical' for $|\text{coeff}|<0.25$. Condone 'strongly' positive skew. Any mention of 'correlation' is B0.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 sub. their values into formula allow use of $s$ but their $\sigma$ or $s$ must be $>0$. A1 for awrt 0.08 but accept 0.085 No fraction
- B1ft for a correct comment compatible with their coefficient. They may say it is "slightly skew" so omit "positive" but do not allow "negative" if coef' +ve

questions.stem: The heights of adult females are normally distributed with mean 160 cm and standard deviation 8 cm.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the probability that a randomly selected adult female has a height greater than 170 cm.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $\mathrm{P}(H>170)=\mathrm{P}\left(Z>\dfrac{170-160}{8}\right)$ [$=\mathrm{P}(Z>1.25)$]. M1: $=1-0.8944$. A1: $=0.1056$ (calc $0.1056498\ldots$), awrt 0.106 (accept 10.6%).
Official notes (completeness pass):
- 1st M1 for attempt at standardising with 170, 160 and 8. Allow $\pm$ i.e. for $\pm\frac{170-160}{8}$
- 2nd M1 for attempting $1-p$ where $0.8<p<1$. Correct answer only 3/3

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Any adult female whose height is greater than 170 cm is defined as tall.

An adult female is chosen at random. Given that she is tall,

(b) find the probability that she has a height greater than 180 cm.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $\mathrm{P}(H>180)=\mathrm{P}\left(Z>\dfrac{180-160}{8}\right)$ [$=1-0.9938$]. A1: $=0.0062$ (calc $0.006209\ldots$), awrt 0.0062 or $\frac{31}{5000}$. M1: $[\mathrm{P}(H>180\,|\,H>170)]=\dfrac{0.0062}{0.1056}$. A1: $=0.0587$ (calc $0.0587760\ldots$), awrt 0.0587 or 0.0588. Condone 5.87% or 5.88% or $\frac{31}{528}$.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- 1st A1 for 0.0062 seen, maybe seen as part of another expression/calculation.
- 2nd M1 using conditional probability with denom = their (a) and num < their denom. Values needed.
- Correct answer only 4/4

parts.label: c
parts.text:
Half of tall adult females have a height greater than $h$ cm.

(c) Find the value of $h$.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $\mathrm{P}(H>h\,|\,H>170)(=0.5)$ or $\dfrac{\mathrm{P}(H>h)}{\mathrm{P}(H>170)}(=0.5)$. A1ft: $[\mathrm{P}(H>h)]=0.5\times\text{'}0.1056\text{'}=0.0528$ (calc $0.0528249\ldots$) or $[\mathrm{P}(H<h)]=0.9472$. M1: attempt to standardise ($\pm$) with 160 and 8 and set equal to $\pm z$ value ($1.56<|z|<1.68$). B1: ($z=$) awrt $\pm1.62$ (seen). A1: $h=$ awrt 173 cm, dependent on both M marks.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- 1st M1 for a correct conditional probability statement. Either line and don't insist on 0.5, ft (a)
- Award M1A1ft for correct evaluation of $0.5\times$their$(a)$ or sight of 0.0528 or better
